capture.description: Test vectors for contract/span-contract.md section 15 (revision 3.2): redaction of captured bodies, the tenant, and Lambda error text. 'capture' and 'tenant' are the options given to the package; defaults apply to everything not given. Both packages must produce exactly 'redacted', 'redacted_count' and 'format' for each body. 'offloaded_size': both packages must set trailbeam.body.offloaded_size to 'expected' (absent when null), with body capture off.

purge.description: Test vectors for contract/span-contract.md section 18 (revision 3.3): the trailbeam purge span. Each case is one PurgeQueue call on 'queue_url'. 'response' is what the call returned: {"ok": true} for success, {"error_code": c} for an SQS error response with code c, or {"thrown": n} for an error named n raised before any response. Each package must emit exactly one span named 'span_name' whose attributes include exactly 'attributes', carry every name in 'present' (values depend on the process) and none in 'absent'. trailbeam.order.issued must be lower than trailbeam.order.returned.

cases.name: success
purge already in progress
error code with a protocol namespace
no response

sns.description: Test vectors for contract/span-contract.md section 21 (revision 3.4): SNS fan-out. 'timestamps': [envelope Timestamp, epoch ms or null]. 'receive': one received message (the SNS envelope is read on every queue); 'message_attributes' are in ReceiveMessage form (a Lambda record has the same with 'stringValue' / 'dataType'); a receive span must carry exactly 'attributes' among the trailbeam.sns.* names. 'inject': one Publish ('entries' has one item, the request) or PublishBatch call; 'results' gives, per entry, 'injected' (the entry gets a trailbeam.publish_id String attribute, a UUID, and the span the same value) or the trailbeam.sns.publish_id_skipped reason; the caller's objects must not change. 'publish': whole spans for calls with injection off: each package must emit one span per item of 'spans', in order, whose attributes include exactly those, carry every name in 'present' and none in 'absent'. A 'Message' written as {"repeat": c, "times": n} stands for the string c repeated n times.

eventbridge.description: Test vectors for contract/span-contract.md section 25 (revision 3.6): EventBridge PutEvents. 'put_events': whole spans of one PutEvents call. Each case has the 'request', and the 'response' or, for a call that failed as a whole, the 'error' code (boto3: a ClientError with that code; Node.js: an error whose name is that code). Each package must emit exactly 'spans', one per request entry in entry order, named 'trailbeam put_event', each with exactly the listed attributes plus the 'present' ones and none of the 'absent' ones. The request must not change.

a source or detail-type over 256 characters is left out
an EventId that is not 1 to 64 letters, digits or - is left out, and the entry is failed
a request with no entries: no span
an EventId with a trailing newline is left out, and the entry is failed

s3.description: Test vectors for contract/span-contract.md section 27 (revision 3.7): S3 uploads. 'uploads': whole spans of one PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload or CopyObject call. Each case has the 'operation', the process's body capture queue list 'body_queues' (section 15.1; a bucket's name in it turns on its object key), the 'request', and the 'response' or, for a call that failed as a whole, the 'error' code (boto3: a ClientError with that code; Node.js: an error whose name is that code). Each package must emit exactly 'spans', named 'trailbeam s3_upload', each with exactly the listed attributes plus the 'present' ones and none of the 'absent' ones, and no attribute value containing 'secret'. The request must not change.
